prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Xenon (제논) itself — the sovereign of the Xenon Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; deep brown skin; diamond-shaped face; medium-sized eyes — long monolid eyes, level outer eye corners; thick straight brows; straight narrow nose; thin long lips; glowing pale ion-blue eyes; sharp winged eyeliner.
Body and hair: lean and long-legged, with a natural neck length build; an asymmetric bob, longer on one side with blunt straight bangs; silver-white hair flashing pale ion-blue at the ends like a strobe.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: one brow slightly raised, attentive eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: xenon: 'the stranger', found in 1898 by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in the last residue of liquefied air, the rarest and heaviest stable noble gas, less than one part in ten million of the air; glows blue in a discharge tube and blazes white in camera flashes and cinema arc lamps; in 1962 Neil Bartlett made it the first noble gas ever to form a compound, an orange-yellow solid with fluorine and platinum; its ions stream as the blue exhaust of deep-space probe engines; a calm, daring wanderer who broke the nobles' rule.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a clockwork gear rig worn on her back over a fitted vest, small brass fittings on arms and legs — the machinery makes the shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: pale ion-blue glow, strobe-flash white, deep space black, a single accent of hexafluoroplatinate orange-gold.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: London in 1898, William Ramsay's laboratory at University College: a clanking air-liquefaction machine of brass coils and pressure gauges, frosted fractional-distillation flasks boiling liquefied air down to its last heavy residue, a glass discharge tube glowing a strange blue, a brass spectroscope showing lines no one had ever seen.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Xe) and atomic number (54) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
